key_insight: This paper argues that language intelligence can be improved by pretraining on visually rich data, not just plain text. By preserving figures, equations, and layout information, models can learn knowledge that is otherwise lost during text-only conversion.
problem_solved: Current foundation-model pretraining often strips away visual cues from documents and web pages, discarding important information encoded in images, formulas, and page structure. The paper tackles how to scale pretraining so models can learn from these visual signals efficiently.
method: Pretrain on visually rich sources such as documents and web pages while retaining non-text visual information.
Learn from multimodal page representations that combine text with figures, equations, and layout cues.
Scale the pretraining pipeline to support large foundation models without relying only on plain-text extraction.
impact: This matters because many high-value domains like scientific publishing, legal documents, and technical web content depend on visual structure as much as text. Practitioners can build models with better document understanding, richer knowledge capture, and improved performance on tasks requiring visual reasoning over text.

paper_title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence
paper_authors: Yiming Zhang, Zhonghan Zhao, Wenwei Zhang, Haiteng Zhao, Tianyang Lin
